criteria.description: A new pure module for incremental coverage judging exists as a sibling of the existing coverage_judge.py / coverage_store.py modules (flat repo-root layout, e.g. an incremental_coverage_judge.py file next to them). At import time it pulls in only the Python standard library — no anthropic, pipecat, fastapi, or other third-party imports at module top level; any Anthropic client is constructed lazily inside a function/method, never at import.
criteria.verifyBy: A hermetic test imports the module and asserts no third-party import happened at module scope (mirroring the existing test_module_has_no_network_or_live_app_imports_at_module_scope pattern — AST-scan of top-level import statements and/or a sys.modules delta showing no anthropic/pipecat/fastapi added by import). Grader reads the module source to confirm any Anthropic client instantiation is inside a function body, not at module scope.

criteria.description: The module defines model and path constants at module scope (mirroring the existing coverage modules' naming conventions) as named, monkeypatchable constants, plus a named LOOKBACK_WINDOW constant defaulting to 4 turns. LOOKBACK_WINDOW carries an explanatory docstring/comment stating it is load-bearing (explanations span turn boundaries) — it is a real named constant, not an inline magic number.
criteria.verifyBy: Grader reads module source confirming LOOKBACK_WINDOW = 4 exists as a documented named constant and that model/path constants exist at module scope as named constants matching the existing modules' style. A hermetic test monkeypatches LOOKBACK_WINDOW at a MID-TRANSCRIPT position (first new turn well clear of the head clamp, i.e. first_new_index strictly greater than any window value under test) and asserts: (a) the number of preceding (lookback) turns selected by the pure request-assembly function equals min(LOOKBACK_WINDOW, first_new_index); (b) raising LOOKBACK_WINDOW selects STRICTLY MORE preceding turns at that mid-transcript position where the head clamp is not in play; (c) the upper bound holds — no selected preceding turn has an index below 0 and the count never exceeds the number of available preceding turns. Model/path constants are only required to be present and monkeypatchable (no live effect exercised this sprint).

criteria.description: The public contract for a single incremental pass is documented (docstring on the entry function plus a typed result structure, e.g. a dataclass) and stable in shape. INPUTS: session turns so far, index of last-judged turn, set of already-covered claim ids, full claim map, and a prompt passed as a versioned parameter (prompt text + version identifier) — the prompt is never hardcoded in the module. OUTPUTS: newly-covered claim ids each with per-claim evidence (cited turn indices + reason), the new last-judged-turn index, the prompt version used, and cost/usage for the pass. This entry path is exercised THIS sprint via an injected fake client (reusing the existing CountingClient/UsageTally style seam); only the real Anthropic transport path and credentialed smoke are deferred.
criteria.verifyBy: Grader reads the entry function signature and docstring / result dataclass confirming all named inputs and outputs are present. A hermetic test with an injected fake client asserts the returned object exposes: newly-covered claim ids, per-claim evidence with cited turns and reason, new last-judged-turn index, the recorded prompt version, and cost/usage fields.

criteria.description: Request-assembly logic — deciding which turns and which claims get sent to the model — is a pure, client-free, I/O-free function testable with no model call. The index space is pinned and documented: the last-judged index and the lookback arithmetic operate in the same turn-index space established by coverage_judge.load_transcript (the committed fixtures are contiguous 0-based, so list position and Turn.index coincide there). Window semantics: it selects all new turns (strictly after the last-judged index) PLUS exactly LOOKBACK_WINDOW turns immediately preceding the first new turn, clamped at the transcript start (index 0) so a near-head pass never under-runs the list; and it excludes every claim already in the covered set from what is sent.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic tests call the pure assembly function directly (no client) and assert: (a) turns sent = new turns plus exactly LOOKBACK_WINDOW preceding turns, clamped at 0 at the transcript head (explicit head-boundary test with last-judged index near 0, asserting count = min(LOOKBACK_WINDOW, first_new_index)); (b) claims sent exclude all ids in the covered set; (c) zero new turns selects no work; (d) all claims covered selects no claims; (e) a c49-shaped distributed-explanation test in which a cited prior turn lies strictly MORE than 1 and AT MOST 4 turns before the first new turn (mirroring the real c49 [4,6,8,14,16] straddle with unrelated turns in between): a window of 1 MISSES that prior turn while LOOKBACK_WINDOW=4 CATCHES it, pinning that 4 specifically is load-bearing. Grader confirms the function takes no client parameter, performs no I/O, and that the documented index space matches load_transcript.

criteria.description: The prompt is echoed through as an input and its version is recorded in the output; the module records which prompt version was used without depending on the prompt's wording. Passing a different prompt string/version changes only what is sent and which version is recorded, not the module's mechanics.
criteria.verifyBy: A hermetic test invokes a pass (via injected fake client) with a given prompt string + version, captures what the fake client received, and asserts the supplied prompt text was used and the returned result records the exact supplied version. A second invocation with a different version records the different version, proving no hardcoding.

criteria.description: All new tests are additive and hermetic; the pinned verifier passes with no regressions. No previously-passing test is broken, and the new incremental-judging test file(s) run and pass under the same verifier.
criteria.verifyBy: Run /Users/mattli/development/voice-tutor/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q from the worktree and assert exit code 0; confirm no previously-passing test regressed (the baseline suite stays green) and that the new incremental-judging test file(s) are collected and pass. No exact pass-count floor is asserted.

criteria.description: Hermetic tests read only the committed repo fixtures under tests/fixtures/coverage/** (specifically tests/fixtures/coverage/transcripts/f6148c26.json and tests/fixtures/coverage/claims/matt-2aa66acc.claims.json) and never open any path under ~/.voice-tutor/. The offline layer stays reproducible without touching the real data directory.
criteria.verifyBy: Grader greps the new test files confirming they reference the tests/fixtures/coverage/** paths and contain no reference to ~/.voice-tutor/ (or an expanded absolute equivalent). A behavioral check (e.g. the tests run with HOME/data dir irrelevant, or an assertion that no such path is opened) confirms the hermetic layer is offline.

criteria.description: The request-assembly function is deterministic and side-effect-free: identical inputs yield identical selection across repeat calls, and it does not mutate any of its inputs — the caller's covered set, the turns list, and the claim map are unchanged after the call. This pins the pure-layer aspect of the monotonic, caller-owned-state and idempotence mechanics for this sprint.
criteria.verifyBy: A hermetic test calls the assembly function twice with identical inputs and asserts the two selections are equal; and it asserts, via equality against pre-call snapshots (copies), that the covered set, turns list, and claim map are unchanged (not mutated) after each call.

criteria.description: Zero-work passes cost nothing OBSERVABLY, and malformed/failed passes degrade to nothing — both without mutating caller inputs. (i) A pass over zero new turns, and a pass where every claim is already covered, each perform NO model call and return empty additions with a zero/absent usage tally — the 'costs nothing' thesis is tied to an observable call count, not merely a present cost field. (ii) A malformed or failed fake-client response during an otherwise-non-trivial pass yields NO newly-covered claim ids (empty additions) and leaves the caller's inputs untouched — the covered set is not shrunk and not grown, and the turns list and claim map are unmutated — with no crash and no partial result. (Only the real Anthropic transport-failure path is deferred to a later sprint.)
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic tests using the CountingClient/UsageTally seam assert: (a) an entry pass over zero new turns invokes the injected fake client ZERO times (call count == 0) and returns empty additions with a zero/absent usage tally; (b) an entry pass where every claim is already covered likewise invokes the fake client ZERO times and returns empty additions with a zero/absent usage tally; (c) a fake client returning a malformed/unparseable response, and a second variant that raises, each cause the pass to return empty additions, not raise, and — via equality against pre-call snapshots — leave the caller's covered set, turns list, and claim map unchanged (no shrink, no mutation).

scope.description: New module lives as a sibling file of coverage_judge.py / coverage_store.py at the repo root; new tests live alongside the existing coverage tests. No other production module is modified. A rename or shared helper may fan out to a small number of dependent files, but the intent is a self-contained new module plus its tests.

No Pipecat imports, no pipeline wiring (bot.py, session lifecycle, frontend untouched), no live UI/polling/meter, no changes to teardown judging, no persistence of live state. IN scope this sprint: skeleton + documented contract + pure request-assembly + a fake-client-injected entry pass returning the full documented output shape (additions, per-claim evidence, new last-judged index, prompt version, cost/usage) and its pure failure-degradation and zero-work no-call behavior, all covered by hermetic tests. DEFERRED to later sprints: the real Anthropic transport-calling path, real transport-failure handling, and the credentialed smoke run.

~/.voice-tutor/ is strictly read-only and must not be touched by hermetic tests at all; the production server at :7860 and sibling worktrees are not touched. No new venv, no pip installs, no new dependencies — stdlib-only at import with a lazy Anthropic client.
